scope_note: Directed fourth-pass model review retains eight bounded estimates grounded in published Douglas County or official national inputs: three presentation-preserving water-consumption conversions, one ECHO DMR-flow annualization, two county-M&O-only gross-levy counterfactuals on exempt personal property, one historical employee-threshold wage-bill sensitivity, and one permit-remodel construction-payroll sensitivity. Every estimate remains unallocated, non-audited, and outside direct-record totals. Tax counterfactuals are not bills, payments, tax avoided, realized abatement, net fiscal benefit, or all-jurisdiction liability; wage and construction results are transferred benchmarks rather than observed Google payroll; DMR flow is not consumption or utility-billed volume. Supplier retention, electricity use/cost, actual public-service cost, and causal county outcomes remain unsupported.

sources.title: Economic impact of Google data centers in Georgia
sources.notes: The Douglas County sustainability page reports water consumption of 305.2 million gallons in 2022 and 345.6 million gallons in 2023. The values are location-level, rounded, and not allocated to an individual building or meter.

sources.title: Google 2025 Environmental Report
sources.notes: The assured location table reports Douglas County 2024 water consumption of 366.9 million gallons, calculated as 444.1 million gallons withdrawal minus 77.2 million gallons discharge. Displayed values are rounded; no building allocation, bill, tariff, or cost is published.

sources.title: Douglas County, Georgia 2024 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report
sources.notes: Exhibit XIII reports county direct maintenance-and-operations millage of 12.313 mills in 2023 and 12.063 mills in 2024. School rates are excluded from the modeled county-only counterfactual.

sources.title: BLS QCEW 2015 annual averages by county and industry
sources.notes: The annual county table reports $684 average weekly wage for Douglas County (area 13097), all ownerships and total covered industries in 2015. This is an all-industry county benchmark, not a Google wage or occupational mix.

sources.title: 2022 Economic Census, Construction: Geographic Area Statistics for the U.S.
sources.notes: The U.S. NAICS 23 row reports $2,920,771,250 thousand in business receipts and $529,751,969 thousand in annual payroll, a 0.1813740015 payroll-to-receipts ratio. It is a national broad-sector benchmark, not a data-center or Douglas County contractor observation.

sources.title: EPA ECHO DMR pollutant-loading report for permit GA0038920
sources.notes: The report identifies Google LLC, NPDES GA0038920, and displays 0.18 MGD average facility flow in 2026. The result is rounded and may reflect an incomplete reporting year; it is not audited annual discharge or utility-billed volume.

estimates.label: 350-employee threshold wage-bill benchmark

period.label: Annualized benchmark at the June 2015 reported employee threshold

scope.label: Google Douglas County facility employee-threshold wage-bill benchmark

interval.interpretation: The 350-employee threshold is multiplied by 52 weeks and 75%, 100%, and 125% of Douglas County's $684 all-industry average weekly wage. This is a benchmark sensitivity, not observed Google payroll or a confidence interval.

parameters.name: reported_employee_threshold

provenance.detail: Operator reported more than 350 existing facility employees; 350 is retained as the threshold

parameters.transformation: Multiplied by weekly wage and 52 weeks

parameters.name: douglas_all_industry_weekly_wage

provenance.detail: 2015 annual-average weekly wage, Douglas County, all ownerships, total covered industries

parameters.transformation: Multiplied by 52 weeks and the employee threshold

provenance.detail: Low transfer sensitivity for an unknown Google occupation and compensation mix
Central transfer of the county all-industry wage
High transfer sensitivity for an unknown Google occupation and compensation mix

estimates.confidence_rationale: The headcount threshold and county wage are public, but the headcount is a point-in-time greater-than statement, the county wage spans all covered industries, and the 2016 local table reports a conflicting 300-person snapshot.
estimates.decision_relevance: Provides a transparent historical wage-bill scale while preserving the absence of Google payroll, occupation, benefit, residence, and annual-average FTE data.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Observed annual Google W-2 payroll, annual-average FTE, occupation and wage distribution, benefits, contractors, worker residence, and reconciliation of 2015 and 2016 headcounts

derivation.formula: 350 employees x $684 average weekly county wage x 52 weeks x wage factor
assumptions: The published 350 value is used as a threshold, not the unknown value above 350.
The Douglas County all-industry weekly wage is a scale benchmark, not Google's actual wage.
The 75%-125% factors illustrate occupational and employer-mix uncertainty rather than statistical confidence.
All 52 weeks are used for annualization; benefits, equity, bonuses, contractors, and residence effects are excluded.
The 2016 300-employee table is treated as a noncomparable warning, not interpolated or averaged.

limitations: Not observed payroll, labor income, total compensation, resident earnings, or current employment.
Headcount may not equal annual-average FTE and may include an unknown workforce definition.
The interval does not encompass uncertainty in the greater-than headcount itself.
estimates.notes: Historical 350-employee threshold wage-bill benchmark only; do not present as Google's payroll or a current recurring contribution.

estimates.label: Permit-remodel direct construction payroll sensitivity

scope.label: Commercial interior-remodel permit 2502392-DC at 300 Riverside Parkway

interval.interpretation: The $249,864.77 administrative permit value is multiplied by the 0.1813740015 national 2022 construction payroll/receipts ratio and 0.5, 1.0, and 1.5 transfer factors. The deliberately wide range is not observed payroll, a true bound, or a confidence interval.

parameters.name: administrative_permit_value
parameters.transformation: Multiplied by the national construction payroll-to-receipts ratio

parameters.name: national_construction_payroll_receipts_ratio

provenance.detail: $529,751,969 thousand annual payroll divided by $2,920,771,250 thousand business receipts for U.S. NAICS 23

parameters.transformation: Transferred to the permitted remodel value

provenance.detail: Low sensitivity for scope, equipment, subcontract, geography, timing, and wage-mix differences
Central unadjusted transfer of the national sector ratio
High sensitivity for scope, equipment, subcontract, geography, timing, and wage-mix differences

estimates.confidence_rationale: The permit value and Census ratio are public, but an administrative remodel valuation is not verified spending and the national broad-construction ratio is not project-, contractor-, or county-specific.
estimates.decision_relevance: Provides a bounded payroll scale for the only valued permit while keeping it separate from project spending, supplier purchases, permanent payroll, and the historical campus buildout.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Contract amount, invoices, payments, equipment exclusion, worker hours, contractor and subcontractor payroll, benefits/proprietor income, worker residence, and local supplier geography

derivation.formula: $249,864.77 permit value x ($529,751,969k payroll / $2,920,771,250k receipts) x transfer factor
assumptions: The administrative permit value is used as a scenario base but is not asserted to equal expenditure.
The 2022 U.S. NAICS 23 payroll/receipts ratio transfers to this small 2025 interior remodel only for scale analysis.
The 0.5-1.5 factors illustrate transfer uncertainty; they are not statistical bounds.
No historical 2006, 2011, or 2015/2016 construction value is inferred.
No indirect, induced, supplier-retention, or resident-worker effect is modeled.

limitations: Not observed payroll, project cost, invoice, contract payment, or local labor income.
The national sector ratio may include a materially different mix of work and establishments.
Permit value may include or exclude equipment and may differ from completed cost.
estimates.notes: Direct payroll sensitivity for permit 2502392-DC only. It must not be expanded to the campus buildout or called observed or local payroll.

estimates.label: Annualized ECHO DMR average facility flow

period.label: Annualized from the 2026 ECHO DMR average facility flow displayed on September 7, 2026

scope.label: Google LLC permitted discharge facility GA0038920 in Lithia Springs

interval.interpretation: Annualization of a displayed 0.18 MGD average using 365 days, with 0.175-0.185 MGD bounds for rounding to two decimal places. It is not a confidence interval or a complete audited 2026 annual total.

parameters.name: echo_dmr_average_facility_flow
parameters.transformation: Multiply by 1,000,000 gallons per million gallons and 365 days

estimates.confidence_rationale: EPA ECHO directly identifies the facility and displayed DMR average, but the current-year reporting window may be incomplete and the page does not establish a full-year audited annual volume or meter reconciliation.
estimates.decision_relevance: Separates a recent reported discharge-flow scale from operator water consumption, permit design capacity, solar procurement, and utility billing.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Complete 2026 DMR reporting period, underlying monthly submissions, outfall/meter reconciliation, sanitary versus cooling components, reuse, and utility-billed sewer volume

derivation.formula: 0.18 million gallons per day x 1,000,000 x 365 days
assumptions: The ECHO 2026 displayed average facility flow applies to permit GA0038920 and is expressed in MGD.
A 365-day year is used only to annualize the displayed daily average.
The displayed 0.18 value is treated as rounded to the nearest 0.01 MGD.
The result remains unallocated and is not substituted for Google-reported consumption or utility billing.

limitations: The 2026 reporting year may be incomplete as of retrieval.
No underlying monthly DMR series or flow-meter audit is reproduced here.
Discharge is not water consumption, withdrawal, sewer bill quantity, or permit design capacity.
estimates.notes: Annualized DMR-flow scale only; do not present as a completed 2026 annual total or add it to water consumption.
